**International Copper Study Group Statistical Committee Fortieth Regular Meeting 9**<sup>**th**</sup> **October 2012, 10.45am-12.45pm Lisbon, Portugal** 

**ICSG/STAT40/1** 

# **Statistical Committee Provisional Agenda** 

## **1. Opening of the Meeting by the Chairman** 

The Chairman will open the 40th regular meeting of the ICSG Statistical Committee 

## **2. Adoption of the Agenda** 

The Chairman will move to adopt the Provisional Agenda 

## **3. Presentation of ICSG Copper Production and Usage Forecast for 2012/2013 and indicative forecast for 2014** 

(Document ICSG/STAT40/2 - to be released 1 week prior to the meeting) 

The forecast (preliminary version) has been developed by the ICSG secretariat based on the Forecast Surveys submitted by member countries and industry and discussions with industry experts. The Chief Statistician, Ms Ana Rebelo, will present the results of the preliminary forecast and explain the main assumptions behind it. 

## **4. Forecasting Forum** 

The ICSG secretariat will open the floor for detailed discussions on the forecast results on a country by country basis.  Delegates will be asked to submit any latest data revisions available for their countries or any other information or data they may have on other specific countries. A version of the forecast will be presented simultaneously on the screen allowing for in-situ revisions. If there are amendments to the forecast the staff will prepare a final version ready for distribution at the EEC meeting in the afternoon. 

## **5. ICSG Statistical Press Release** 

(Document ICSG/STAT40/3 – Draft version to be made available at the meeting) 

A draft of the press release summarizing the forecast results will be jointly prepared by the Chief Statistician and the Chairman. This document will be distributed at the meeting. Delegates will be invited to analyse it and present their comments or suggestions before its final approval. 

## **6. Copper Refined Usage in the EU: Current Situation and Outlook** 

In 2011, EU copper refined usage represented 17% of total world refined usage. While lower than the 29% share the EU had in 2000, it remains the second leading consuming region and its impact on the world copper market is substantial.  In addition, the EU is an important market for finished products containing copper (manufactured within the EU or imported from other regions). However, the current weak economic situation and uncertainty in some EU countries resulting from sovereign debt issues, austerity measures, high unemployment rates, an unstable euro and the banking crisis are having an impact on the copper industry. Dr Mark Loveitt, Secretary General of the International Wrought Copper Council, will speak about the current situation and outlook for refined copper demand in the EU. 

## **7. Outlook for Chinese Copper Usage in 2012 and 2013** 

In 2011, China refined usage represented 40% of the world total usage. In the first half of 2012 Chinese apparent usa

ge grew by 27% compared with that in the same period of 2011 owing to a 80% increase in net imports of refined copper.  However, anecdotal evidence suggests that the 

high import level was accompanied by increased inventories held in bonded warehouses.  Although the accumulated net imports in the first months of 2012 were higher than in the same period of 2011, we have witnessed since March 2012 a downward trend in monthly net import volumes. Other signs of weakness are arising in China.  Ms Li Lan, Head of Marketing Research at BGRIMM, will speak about the current situation and outlook of the refined copper usage in China. 

## **8. Forecast Comparisons and Accuracy of ICSG Forecast** 

(Document ICSG/STAT40/4) 

The ICSG Chief Statistician will present the results of the comparison analysis between previous supply-demand forecasts and actual data. This comparison exercise is an indicative tool to assess the validity of ICSG projections by identifying the main reasons for over/under estimates for production and usage. ICSG forecasts of production and usage for 2011 will be compared with actual ICSG data results. 

The accuracies of the projections produced by the Study Group are highly dependent on the inputs of the twice-yearly forecasts received from each Study Group member country. Therefore member countries should ensure maximum rigor in developing the forecast data provided to the ICSG secretariat.  Unforeseen factors such as strikes, operational failures or natural disasters and the ability to adjust for them also have an important impact of the validity of the forecast. 

## **9. Report on progress in the 2012/2013 ICSG Statistical Activities and Projects Work Program** 

(Document ICSG/STAT40/5) 

The secretariat will provide a report on progress in relation to the activities in the approved 2012/2013 Statistics Work Program. 

Delegates are invited to discuss the Work Program and may wish to suggest additional topics. 

## **10. Other business** 

## **11. Arrangements for the Chairman’s Report** 

A report of the meeting will be jointly prepared by the secretariat and the Chairman.
